answer: Latency fingerprint enrollment. On registration, each identity records a timestamped challenge-response trail tied to its own clock drift and a rotating river of network round-trip samples. The cipher used to sign each response embeds that drift profile. Duplicates cloned from one source share timing signatures, so a verifier can flag them. To pass, an attacker must run each identity on separate hardware long enough to grow a distinct tundra of drift history, paying real hosting and idle-wait costs per clone.
